authors: Stien N; Riiser A; Shaw MP; Saeterbakken AH; Andersen V
title: Effects of climbing- and resistance-training on climbing-specific performance: a systematic review and meta-analysis
main_finding: Resistance training may improve climbing-related outcomes versus climbing alone; the intervention base is small.
limitations: Only eleven studies; five entered the meta-analysis; protocols heterogeneous.

authors: Woollings KY; McKay CD; Emery CA
title: Risk factors for injury in sport climbing and bouldering: a systematic review of the literature
main_finding: The review identified possible risk factors; injury-prevention findings were inconclusive.
limitations: Underlying evidence was not robust and modifiable risk factors require prospective study.

title: A Finger in the Game: Sport-Specific Finger Strength Training and Onset of Injury
main_finding: Associations differed by experience; less experienced high-level climbers warrant caution with fingerboard loads.
limitations: Cross-sectional self-report cannot establish causality or a safe threshold.

authors: Langer K; Simon C; Wiemeyer J
title: Strength Training in Climbing: A Systematic Review
journal: Journal of Strength and Conditioning Research
main_finding: Twelve studies showed positive effects across strength and performance outcomes, with trends rather than a universal best protocol.
limitations: Only twelve heterogeneous studies; trends do not establish one optimal dose.

authors: Quarmby A; Zhang M; Geisler M; Javorsky T; Mugele H; Cassel M; Lawley J
title: Risk factors and injury prevention strategies for overuse injuries in adult climbers: a systematic review
journal: Frontiers in Sports and Active Living
main_finding: Higher intensity, bouldering, crimp grip and previous injury were associated with overuse injury; several other factors were conflicting.
limitations: Associations do not establish causality or safe thresholds; prevention research remains limited.

title: Comparison of the Effects of Three Hangboard Strength and Endurance Training Programs on Grip Endurance in Sport Climbers
main_finding: Maximal and intermittent dead-hang groups improved grip endurance over eight weeks; intermittent training improved earlier in this small sample.
limitations: Small advanced-only sample and no non-training control; cannot generalize dose to novices.

authors: Stien N; Pedersen H; Vereide VA; Saeterbakken AH; Hermans E; Kalland J; Schoenfeld BJ; Andersen V
title: Effects of Two vs. Four Weekly Campus Board Training Sessions on Bouldering Performance and Climbing-Specific Tests in Advanced and Elite Climbers
journal: Journal of Sports Science and Medicine
main_finding: Two or four weekly distributions with matched volume produced different improvements versus control, without a clear difference between trained groups.
limitations: Very small groups, five-week intervention and advanced/elite population; no basis for novice prescription.

authors: Langer K; Simon C; Wiemeyer J
title: Physical performance testing in climbing-A systematic review
journal: Frontiers in Sports and Active Living
main_finding: Sixty-three tests with nonuniform procedures were found; reporting of test quality and samples was often insufficient.
limitations: Heterogeneity prevents precise universal test recommendations.
